parsed.explanation: Combined regime creates high, near-severe visitor exposure. National document policy forces birth-sex markers, allows visa refusal and permanent-fraud findings when records conflict, and has stranded trans travellers. State law imposes birth-sex facility, shelter and prison placement; criminalises bathroom trespass after refusal; penalises impersonator performance; and has a documented arrest. Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. Counterterrorism language frames pro-trans activism as hostile. Minor care bans and school outing laws sharply raise family travel risk. Some litigation and partial national protections exist, but no operative traveller-facing remedy is documented. No execution is credibly threatened, but arrest, humiliation, denial of care, custody abuse and forced outing are credible if discovered.

entry_documents.exposure: New passports/visas require assigned sex; no new X marker; screening can refuse or flag misrepresentation, and lifetime fraud may be considered; trans travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; litigation and legal-aid FAQ are documented; some executive orders are challenged or enjoined, but not reliably protective for travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at border can trigger secondary screening, visa denial, removal risk, investigation, and later facility or custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; national prison conversion policies and state birth-sex prison placement; documented bathroom arrest led to men’s-ward detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Pretrial release in one arrest is documented; no protective custody, trans-specific detention protocol, or reliable oversight mitigation is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or facility disputes can become custody; birth-sex placement can expose the traveller to assault, care denial and coercive treatment.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State bars birth-mismatched bathrooms, changing rooms, shelters and prison placement; national order bars congruent use in government-funded single-sex facilities; criminal trespass with refusal; one documented arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states lack mapped bans, but local ordinances can be preempted; no operative public-accommodation right is documented for a visitor in this division.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National policy plus state criminalisation makes routine restroom/changing-room use a continuous, inescapable exposure wherever the traveller is outed.

care_services.exposure: Minor gender-affirming care is barred and must be withdrawn; inmate care is banned; national funding and reimbursement hostility restricts services; crisis services were narrowed.
care_services.protection: Not documented for traveller continuity; adult private care access is not addressed in the dossier.
care_services.interaction: Seeking HRT or clinic/school care can out a minor, trigger reporting, fraud suspicion, or care denial; absence of documented adult import rules is not safety.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism prioritises identification of ‘radically pro-transgender’ groups; reward memo references radical gender ideology; state criminalises impersonator performance and school outing laws exist.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Some orders are blocked or challenged; national employment discrimination precedent remains; a drag-law suit is ongoing but unresolved.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing can widen discretionary stops, document scrutiny, service refusals and social license for hostility toward visibly trans travellers.

minors_guardians.exposure: Schools must out students requesting different names or pronouns; minors’ care is banned; parents/guardians can face regret suits, penalties and investigation; national directive targets teachers facilitating transition.
minors_guardians.protection: No traveller or family shield statute is documented; marriage recognition and employment precedent do not create a visitor-facing mitigation here.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor risks forced outing at school, clinic, ID checks, and suspicion of aiding prohibited care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented pattern of service refusals, beatings and harassment; panic defence available; police/legal officials reportedly indifferent; state hate-crime law lacks gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and employment precedent may allow some recourse, but effectiveness for visitors and this division is not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street hostility can escalate into police contact, document checks, misgendered custody, inadequate investigation or retaliation for reporting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Patchwork enforcement across states; ongoing suits; unresolved status of recent facility, shelter, prison and drag provisions; application to everyday trans presentation is partly unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Court challenges, ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ and some injunctions are documented, but no reliable operative remedy for a short-term traveller is shown.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Legal uncertainty can reduce or intensify risk by date and location; officers and providers may apply restrictive interpretations before appeals conclude.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.15-A because the dossier does not document routine months-long pretrial custody or capital exposure for visitors. It remains close to the severe boundary through passport/visa fraud screening, birth-sex facility criminalisation, immigration custody abuse, prison placement and official threat framing.

Slightly below 0.25-C. Both impose birth-sex prison placement and criminalised presentation. This regime adds national entry/fraud screening, documented bathroom arrest, impersonator-performance felony exposure, minor-out and care-ban layers, and immigration custody sexual abuse, without the same explicit documented prison-assault frequency.

Materially below 0.35-A. 0.35-A involves exclusion and humiliation without credible imprisonment; here birth-sex facilities are criminal in some settings, prisons and shelters are birth-sex placed, and immigration custody includes severe abuse, creating a more catastrophic if discovered consequence set.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is an enforced birth-sex document and facility system. Border screening can convert a presentation/document conflict into visa refusal or permanent-fraud suspicion; any resulting encounter with police, immigration, corrections or clinics channels the traveller into birth-sex placement where abuse and conversion are documented. State criminal laws make restroom use, shelters and impersonator performance prosecutable, so ordinary travel can escalate. Minor care and school outing rules add family exposure. Partial national rights and litigation exist, but they are not shown to protect visitors. Risk is high rather than maximum: no execution is credibly documented, but detention, assault, service denial, forced outing and stranded removal are plausible.
